communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the Presidential Records Act (44 U.S.C. § 2201 et seq.), I hereby request access to all textual records, visitor entry logs, protocol lists, and event rosters referring or relating to:

SUBJECT INDIVIDUAL: 

Günter Straßmeir (transliterations: Gunter Strassmeir, Gunter Strassmeier, Gunther Strassmeir; DOB: June 20, 1929 – DOD: December 24, 2009), former Parliamentary State Secretary to Chancellor Helmut Kohl and member of the Berlin House of Representatives. 

For guidance, here's the German Wikipedia entry: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCnter_Stra%C3%9Fmeir Strassmeir was a close confidant and former chief of staff to Helmut Kohl.

White House Visitor Records / WAVES Logs (or predecessor/functional-equivalent system): Any record of entry, scheduled appointment, or security clearance pass for Günter Straßmeir attending meetings, receptions, or bilateral briefings at the White House complex, for the full period January 20, 1993, through January 20, 1997 [see note below].

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA / Archival Record Request: FAA Great Lakes Region NTAP/PDARS Radar Logs (September 11, 2001)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request access to and copies of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Great Lakes Region Air Traffic Control records preserved within the 9/11 Commission files or general FAA record groups (Record Group 237).

Specifically, request includes:

National Track Analysis Program (NTAP) or Performance Data Analysis Reporting System (PDARS) automated radar track data extractions covering the airspace sectors controlling eastern Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota, and Wisconsin between 12:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC on September 11, 2001.

Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) Command Center Logs and military coordinator logbooks from the Minneapolis ARTCC (ZMP) for flights utilizing refueling tracks AR-310 or AR-610 during the national airspace ground stop window.

Sector voice recording logs or transcripts for the ZMP sectors handling military tactical traffic with callsigns "CLEAN" [01-10], "AMC 319", or military fighter tracks matching Lt. Col. Gibney's mission trajectory.

REQUEST FOR NEWS MEDIA STATUS & FEE WAIVER

1. Representative of the News Media Status

I request that I be categorized as a representative of the news media for fee assessment purposes under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(II) and 32 C.F.R. § 286.12.

I am an independent journalist conducting an investigative historical report regarding the air defense and aerial refueling infrastructure in operation on September 11, 2001.

The requested records are not sought for commercial use. They will be used purely in my editorial capacity for a forthcoming, deep-dive investigative feature to be published on critic.markciubal.com. This platform regularly publishes analytical, data-driven investigative journalism regarding historical aviation, military records, and public safety data.

As a modern independent publisher, I perform the traditional journalistic functions of gathering information, exercising editorial judgment to analyze and synthesize raw data, and distributing the finalized work to the public.

2. Request for a Public Interest Fee Waiver

Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii), I request a complete waiver of all search, duplication, and review fees because disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest.

Understanding Government Operations: The requested FAA radar extractions and military squadron flight logs shed direct light on the operations, response times, and coordination of the Department of Defense and the Federal Aviation Administration during a critical turning point in national security history.

Significant Contribution to Public Understanding: There is an active, ongoing historical debate regarding the precise timelines, geographic ranges, and interception metrics achieved on September 11, 2001. The public currently lacks access to these raw data-extraction logs and squadron records. Publishing a synthesized, mathematically verified analysis of these flight envelopes on critic.markciubal.com will significantly inform public understanding by replacing administrative ambiguity with verifiable physical data.

No Commercial Interest: I have no commercial motive. This investigation is entirely for independent educational, historical, and journalistic purposes.

If this request for news media status or a fee waiver is denied, please notify me immediately before incurring any fees exceeding $25.00.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mark Daniel Ciubal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I. Request Scope & Description of Records

I request copies of all records created, received, or maintained within National Security Council (NSC) channels, or transmitted to/from NSC staff by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) or its Bureau for Europe and Eurasia (E&E), between April 6, 2011, and December 31, 2012, concerning telecommunications development, critical infrastructure security, and internet connectivity in Georgia and Armenia following the April 6, 2011, fiber-optic line severance outside Tbilisi.

For context, an elderly woman collecting copper in the hills outside of Tbilisi in April of 2011 disabled Armenia's internet connectivity:
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/apr/06/georgian-woman-cuts-web-access

Specifically, this request includes:

● NSC briefing memoranda, situation reports, and correspondence discussing the April 2011 fiber-optic severance and its effect on Armenian internet connectivity.

● Correspondence between NSC staff (e.g., the Senior Director for Russian and Eurasian Affairs) and USAID's Bureau for Europe and Eurasia regarding telecommunications sector resilience, broadband access, or critical infrastructure security in Georgia and Armenia.

● Interagency or bilateral correspondence discussing regional reliance on single-channel transit corridors (such as Armenian routes transiting Georgia or Iran).

● Any records reflecting U.S. Embassy Tbilisi or U.S. Embassy Yerevan reporting on the incident that was forwarded to or discussed within NSC channels.

II. Suggested Search Terms & Parameters

To assist your search, please query electronic and paper systems (including text collections, briefing books, and email databases) using the following keyword clusters:

III. Date Range

IV. Format Request
